newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Ladbroke calls sold against stockholding.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Ladbroke calls sold against stockholding.

text.p: UK equity options traded quietly on Monday as traders became wary of taking very large positions at current high levels of the stock market, dealers said.
In the event, traders restricted their involvement to a maximum of a few hundred contracts in any one options class.
The main deal in leisure and hotels company Ladbroke group was the sale of 250 May 240 calls at 10-1/2p which dealers believe was a hedge against buying the underlying stock at 243p.
If Ladbroke shares stay flat or rise only modestly the short calls should increase the return from only holding the shares.

This is because if the share price only goes up a little by May expiry, the calls will be assigned and the trader will have to sell Ladbroke shares at 240p but he will get to keep the 10-1/2p from having originally sold the calls.
And if the share price falls, then the short calls will offer up to 10-1/2p protection against a loss in the stockholding.
By 1325 GMT, Ladbroke shares had lost 2p to 241p.
Call options were also sold as the main deal in oil major Shell Transport & Trading in which 250 April 1150 calls were sold at 8p.

On the other hand, expectations of greater volatility over the next few months may have been behind the deal in retailer Marks & Spencer in which 150 July 500 puts and calls were bought at 27p and 22p each.
Marks & Spencer shares gained 5-1/2p to 496p and for the deal to make a profit by expiry the shares need to either go below 451p or above 549p.
